title: Xbox CEO Plays Coy About Whether Elder Scrolls 6 Will Skip PlayStation
event_sentences: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has suggested Microsoft could make more exclusive games again , but will The Elder Scrolls 6 be among them? We still don't know, but that's the question the BBC asked Sharma at Gamescom this week. But first, Sharma discussed her thoughts generally about exclusives, and how every platform, in her estimation, needs some form of exclusive content to grow.

"We are increasingly going to be one of the largest platforms in the world. Every platform needs some form of exclusive experiences and content," she said. "And so, what we've shared is Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork [Revolution will be exclusive on console to Xbox]. We're going to do the best we can to continue to do that, all in context of the business being healthy, and so we have to balance that."

Pressed to say if it is a "priority" to make The Elder Scrolls 6 exclusive to Xbox on console, Sharma smiled and said, "It's a beautiful game." Sharma recently visited the developers at Bethesda and offered an update on how the game was progressing . During her visit, protestors came to Bethesda's offices to drag Sharma for her decision to lay off thousands of Xbox developers , including people working on The Elder Scrolls 6.
Due to these layoffs and other cuts, staffers at Bethesda are facing "crushing morale" and fears of more delays.

In terms of Microsoft's approach exclusive games going forward, the team has said it will honor existing agreements for Xbox-made games that were previously announced as multiplatform releases. The Elder Scrolls 6 was announced in 2018, but at the time, Bethesda did not confirm platform details. Microsoft acquired Bethesda in 2021, and documents from the Microsoft vs. FTC case said The Elder Scrolls 6 was not planned for PS5 .

Former Xbox boss Phil Spencer, for his part, said in 2021 that making games exclusive to Xbox is "not about punishing any other platform." He also alluded to the possibility of The Elder Scrolls 6 being exclusive to Xbox.

"In order to be on Xbox, I want us to be able to bring the full complete package of what we have. And that would be true when I think about The Elder Scrolls 6," he said. "That would be true when I think about any of our franchises."

Spencer spearheaded the effort to bring more Xbox games to rival platforms in a bid to make more money. He left Xbox earlier this year, and one of Sharma's first moves was to tell fans how important exclusives are to the business . Gears of War: E-Day, which launches this October, was reportedly planned for PS5 before Microsoft opted to make it exclusive on console to Xbox.
Despite being announced more than eight years ago, The Elder Scrolls 6 still has no release date or official details.

title: Devolver Digital Reveals Its GTA 6 Competitor, And It’s A Remaster Of A Nonexistent Remake
event_sentences: Few game companies are brave enough to go head-to-head with the release of Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 , but that's exactly what publisher Devolver Digital is doing with the launch of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed on November 19.

So what is Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, actually? It's a Game Boy Color-style 2D platformer coming to Steam from developer Doinksoft, the studio behind 2D sidescrollers like Gato Roboto and Gunbrella . Volvy himself is a rat-esque (I think?) creature with one big hand and one small hand.

It's all a little absurd, but that's also what makes it fun. While much of the marketing and the entire premise of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed comes off as a meta-video-game-industry joke, the actual game on display in its debut trailer looks like a rollicking good time.

Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is immediately reminiscent of its Game Boy Color-era inspirations, with a vibrant art style, a popping soundtrack, and kinetic movement. Volvy can dash through the air with his giant fist, burrow underground, or hover like a helicopter using his tail, and the trailer shows how all these abilities can all be chained together.

GTA 6 will certainly be hogging the headlines when it releases in November, but the open-world crime simulator isn't everyone's cup of tea, is $80 (or $100) , and isn't releasing on PC at launch. Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, at only $5, offers a nice bit of counterprogramming then for those who are looking for something else to do November 19.
Surprisingly, Volvy isn't the only one bold enough to release on the same day as GTA 6. The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ Online, a port adding online co-op, is also releasing November 19.

title: Exterminauts Devs Talk Helldivers Comparisons And How It Separates Itself
event_sentences: "Our game is not war: It's work," Regimbart said. "It's a workplace that fights back. So there's a thematic difference that we don't want it kind of, to be too heavy on the player--to make it feel like everything is ominous and dire. You're just here to do your 9-5 and get back out."
Regimbart also said that the team felt like it could actually make some improvements to certain aspects of Helldivers, particularly regarding the progression system.

title: You Can Pet (And Scold, You Monster) The Dog In GTA 6
event_sentences: Scolding a dog is probably exactly what it sounds like, though we didn't see it in action. Maybe there's a dog behavior mechanic and scolding helps steer them right? The Study option appears borrowed from Red Dead Redemption 2, which allowed you to study wild animals. That may indicate GTA 6 will allow you to study a variety of creatures, not just dogs. A New York Times report further detailed that you can buy treats for dogs at shops and give them out.

title: GTA 6 Skipping PC At Launch And Having No Online Right Away Is Good, Helldivers Boss Says
event_sentences: The CEO of Helldivers studio Arrowhead Game Studios has commented on the upcoming launch of GTA 6 , saying he's happy there will be no PC version or online mode at launch, because that will help Helldivers 2 "keep crushing it."

In a statement to press, Sham Jorjani said Rockstar makes "ridiculous, high-effort stuff, and it's awesome that games like this get made." He said he's selfishly happy that the game won't be on PC at launch, nor will there be an online mode right away.
"It means Helldivers 2 gets to keep crushing it in our own space, and is also why it won’t be the all consuming behemoth everyone’s worried about," he said.

Rockstar has confirmed GTA 6 will launch on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, but the developer has not said a word about a possible PC edition. Additionally, Rockstar has said GTA 6 is a "single-player experience," but the company has not confirmed outright that there won't be an online mode at launch.

It's expected Rockstar will evolve GTA Online in some form for GTA 6 , but we don't know anything about that yet. With GTA 5, the game launched first on console before later coming to PC. For GTA 6, it's expected the game will also eventually come to PC. Additionally, it won't be unprecedented if GTA 6 launches with no online mode, as GTA 5 also launched without one.
"They have the confidence and freedom to spend a decade doing things the old-school way because they know the core game will deliver. It’s going to raise the bar for sure," he said.
The "Extended Look" for GTA 6 aired today, August 27, on Netflix. For more, be sure to read GameSpot’s breakdown of  how to watch and what to expect from the GTA 6 Extended Look event .

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. It’s coming to market with an incredible amount of hype behind it, in part because fans have been  waiting 13 years for the sequel to GTA 5 .

title: GTA 6 Returns To Six-Star Wanted Levels
event_sentences: A logo showed in the GTA 6 trailer also suggests there will be icons for specific crimes that players commit. The full details aren't available, however, but it makes sense that Rockstar would evolve the wanted system in some form.
Keep checking back with GameSpot for lots more on GTA 6. The game launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

title: GTA 6 Map Is 3X Bigger Than Red Dead Redemption 2’s
event_sentences: Rockstar has shared more details about its long-awaited and heavily hyped Grand Theft Auto 6 , and one key piece of information is that the game's map is apparently three times bigger than Red Dead Redemption 2's. The game takes players back to Vice City, a stand-in for Miami. Players will also be able to explore the surrounding areas.

A New York Times report featuring interviews with Rockstar's developers said, "The overall map, the studio said, is three times as large as the playable area of its previous game, Red Dead Redemption 2."
Additionally, the report said GTA 6 has "well over 600,000 animations," which compares to 55,000 for GTA 5 and 300,000 in Red Dead Redemption 2.

“Every room in the game, somebody thought about this,” Rockstar North boss Aaron Garbut said. “Who’s sitting where, what they’re drinking, the marks that are left on the table. The pictures on the wall will have the people that are in that room, with their tattoos on their arms and their family behind them. That whole thing has been made, and built, and photographed, and placed in this random room in a random building in a huge city, in a world.”
Other GTA 6 details that have been confirmed recently include how a playthrough of the main game can take 80 hours , the game returning to six-star wanted levels , and how you can pet the dog .
Keep checking back with GameSpot for lots more on GTA 6. The game launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

title: GTA 6 Story Is About “Whether Love Can Survive Through This Storm”
event_sentences: Grand Theft Auto VI has finally had its big gameplay reveal. That included more details about the story, which centers heavily on the relationship between Jason and Lucia, and how it'ss impacted by their life of crime.

That relationship is front and center in the gameplay, which lets you switch seamlessly between them. Elsewhere in the report, Nelson says that the two could be lovers or simply partners in crime, and that will be up to the player. To maintain the relationship they'll have to spend time together, like hanging out and responding to texts.
"It's new for G.T.A., this idea of your actions having meaning in terms of how you treat your partner or how violent you are," Nelson said.

title: GTA 6 Has A Red Dead 2 Honor-Style System Tracking How Violent You Are
event_sentences: Following Grand Theft Auto 6's over-the-top Netflix gameplay reveal , Rockstar Games detailed one of the game's most important systems. Building on the traditional Wanted system from previous Grand Theft Auto titles and the Honor system from Red Dead Redemption 2, GTA 6 introduces a Criminal Profile system that tracks how violently players handle their crime sprees.

"This is a story about a couple on the run. We have tried to make the systems and the design support our narrative when and wherever possible," Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson told IGN . "Meaning, if you hit and run, commit a crime and run, get into trouble and move on before the cops get there, and you don’t start shooting people, don't start escalating – which you absolutely can do if you want to – but if you don’t, you’re generally going to be fine."

If you enjoy role-playing as a criminal in Red Dead Redemption 2 or any of GTA Online's NoPixel servers, this Criminal Profile system seems made for you. Grand Theft Auto 6 is still set to launch for PS5 and Xbox Series X on November 19, something reaffirmed by Rockstar in this gameplay reveal and its response to recent gameplay leaks .

title: GTA 6’s Jason Has A Case Of Bane-itis
event_sentences: Netflix's extended Grand Theft Auto 6 preview has arrived, and players are already dissecting the footage to glean new details about Rockstar Games' heavily anticipated sequel. So far, the response has been largely positive except in regards to the voice of Jason Duval, the game's co-leading antihero.

One of the common complaints about Jason on social media is that he's difficult to understand for some listeners. This has drawn some comparison's to Tom Hardy's nearly incompressible Bane voice in trailers for The Dark Knight Rises. It's unknown if Rockstar will take any measures to adjust Jason's voice to make it easier to comprehend--as director Christopher Nolan did for Bane in the theatrical cut--but the prevailing sentiment online isn't in favor of Jason's vocals.

Prior to the new preview event, Rockstar called the recent GTA 6 leaks " heartbreaking for our team ." Several years ago, Rockstar discovered the identity of a previous GTA 6 leaker and initiated legal proceedings against them. For now, the current leaker's true identity is unknown.
Grand Theft Auto 6 will be released on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19.

title: GTA 6’s Jason And Lucia Aren’t Necessarily A Couple
event_sentences: GTA 6 's main characters are Jason and Lucia, and while previous trailers have shown them in some steamy scenes, their relationship will be defined by how people play, not by a strict story mandate.
“It’s new for GTA, this idea of your actions having meaning in terms of how you treat your partner or how violent you are ,” Nelson said.

Rockstar has also said GTA 6's story is about "whether love can survive through this storm." This was alluded to in GTA 6's first trailer. It featured the Tom Petty song "Love Is A Long Road." Petty sings about a girl he knew who “said she cared about me” but opines that “love is a long road” with many twists and turns.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. We learned a lot more about the game today, including how the map is 3X bigger than Red Dead Redemption 2's and that a playthrough can be 80 hours long . The game also brings back six-star wanted levels and that you can pet the dog .

title: GTA 6’s Big Netflix Extended Look: All The Things We Learned
event_sentences: After literal years of waiting since the game's official announcement, Rockstar has finally pulled back the curtain on Grand Theft Auto 6's gameplay. The Netflix-exclusive Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look gave us a chance to see the game's open-world activities, combat, story missions, characters, vehicles, and much more, which just makes the wait for November 19 even more excruciating. Below, we've rounded up our coverage so you can learn about whatever it is you're most interested in regarding GTA 6.

After being absent in Grand Theft Auto 5, the six-star Wanted system returns in GTA 6. It's not entirely clear what this entails, but the crimes you've been caught committing are visible via icons under the stars.

No surprise here if you've played GTA 5 or Red Dead Redemption 2, but Grand Theft Auto 6 could take you a long time to complete. Rockstar North's Rob Nelson estimated his playthrough at about 80 hours, focused mostly on the main narrative and narrative-based optional content.

The core of Grand Theft Auto 6's story is the relationship between Lucia and Jason. The two don't necessarily have to be in a romantic relationship, and can exist as platonic partners if you so choose, but the pair, together, is crucial to the story.
No microtransactions or generative AI
Grand Theft Auto 6, at least the single-player game releasing in November, will not feature any microtransactions. Additionally, Rockstar says no generative AI was used in its creation.

Returning from San Andreas is a very-evolved physical-fitness system. Working out as Jason and Lucia will cause them to build more muscle, while eating unhealthy food will make them gain fat. If you don't take time to rest, you'll also find it detrimentally affects their health.

title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Will Have No Microtransactions Or Generative AI
event_sentences: Grand Theft Auto VI. It's the most anticipated video game of the year, and possibly of all time. Netflix just aired a 27-minute extended trailer, and you've likely read multiple stories about it right here on this site since. Multiple media outlets are now talking about recent visits to Rockstar North in Scotland, and according to one source, GTA VI won't have any microtransactions at launch, and no generative AI was used in its development.

Speaking on the Kinda Funny Gamecast, Kinda Funny's Andy Cortez and Greg Miller revealed that they asked Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson about the potential for microtransactions in GTA, as well as the use of generative AI in its development. Both reported that the answer to both questions was simply "no."
"Can you use your own real-world money to buy things in the game? No monetization," Cortez said. "I asked point blank, 'is AI in the game?' No AI," Miller continued.

The lack of generative AI was also reported by The New York Times in its Grand Theft Auto VI feature posted earlier today. "Grand Theft Auto VI, Rockstar said, has well over 600,000 animations, compared with 55,000 animations in Grand Theft Auto V and 300,000 animations in Red Dead Redemption 2," the article said, which also confirmed that Rockstar "emphasized the new game’s human-made craft."

title: Stealing Cars In GTA 6 Is Probably More Complicated Than You Expected
GTA 6 NPCs Will Notice If You’re Carrying A Weapon In Public
event_sentences: According to a GTA 6 preview in The New York Times , "a player in this one cannot whip out a shotgun or a rocket launcher and walk down the street without expecting the non-player characters to call the police."

As disclosed in Netflix's extended GTA 6 preview special, the game has restored the six-star Wanted level to the franchise. Presumably players will get into more trouble for firing a rocket launcher than simply holding one. But allowing the NPCs to behave more realistically to potential threats adds a new aspect that players will have to consider going forward.

Although the apparent vocal stylings of the game's male antihero, Jason, have been negatively received , players have praised GTA 6's ability to interact with dogs and its potentially complex love story between Jason and his co-lead, Lucia.
Grand Theft Auto 6 will be released on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19.

title: Gears Of War: E-Day Had To Solve One Big Lore Problem –  How Do You Get A Lancer Into The Game?
event_sentences: When Gears of War first debuted in the Xbox 360 generation, it introduced the world to the majesty of the Lancer weapon. A gun with a brutally effective chainsaw mounted to it, the Lancer has become the defining symbol of the franchise, and in Gears of War: E-Day , players will get to see just how that weapon came to be.

"Wherever possible, we've just done everything we can to respect the canon, right? The scene where Tai uses a chainsaw in a grocery store to kill a Locust is part of the creation story that was in a book, but we've lifted it--like all the dialogue--everything is intact in our game," creative director Matt Searcy said to GameSpot. "So even if we have to do like a small retcon, we just lift it and drop. We took the moment, we took the dialogue, we took everything about it and just said if we have to make a change, we're going to respect it as much as we possibly can, and if we need to connect the dots between two things, we're going to."

"We have to have a Lancer in this game. In the lore, it's created a year after E-Day by Marcus' father, so we find ways--like we revealed in our campaign preview where a prototype is built around E-Day--so we can feed into all of those things. It just takes a little bit of care and attention, and then there's usually a great creative solution to be able to respect all of the hard work that's come before and all the things the fans are deeply attached to."

The book that helped inspire the story of Gears of War: E-Day is the 2008 novel Gears of War: The Aspho Fields by Karen Traviss. In it, Gear soldier Tai Kaliso uses a power saw in combat, and that action eventually goes on to inspire the creation of the chainsaw attachment for Lancer rifles. The book also covers the battle in which Dominic Santiago's brother, Carlos, dies, giving The Coalition an established starting point for building Marcus and Dom’s relationship throughout E-Day.

"What it gave us was a really rich jumping-off point," Searcy explained. "So we knew E-Day is a plot point, two-thirds of the population dies, the monsters come out of the ground, and it's a cool concept. But we needed something rich for the characters to be based on, and that gave us a really strong starting point in terms of understanding where Marcus and Dom were before this game."

While the story campaign has been a big focus for the early marketing of Gears of War: E-Day, we're not entirely convinced yet if it'll tell the definitive Gears story that sets up the entire franchise. The multiplayer might be where this prequel truly shines--especially with the overhauled movement systems--and you can check it all out for yourself when Gears of War: E-Day launches on October 6 for Xbox Series X|S and PC.

title: Hellraiser: Revival Is More Than Just Cenobites and Gore – 10 Things We Learned From Saber Interactive
event_sentences: October wouldn't feel right without a spooky game or two, and Hellraiser: Revival is shaping up to be a terrifying-- and horny --dive into the nightmarish fiction of author Clive Barker. So far, the game is looking like the kind of Hellraiser experience that defined the franchise throughout the '80s and early '90s, and at Gamescom, Saber Interactive sat down with GameSpot to talk about the game, how far they're willing to go to nail the vibe of Hellraiser , and more.
Hellraiser: Revival launches for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S on October 8.

The legendary creator of Hellraiser needed some convincing before he started collaborating with Saber Interactive, but once he was assured that the developers had a grasp of the Hellraiser franchise, he gave the studio the freedom to tell their own tale within that dark universe. "Clive Barker was such a permissive partner to work with," narrative director Anthony De Fault said. "He was really supportive of our ideas. He basically just wanted to make sure we understood Hellraiser as a franchise, and then, once he knew that we had the, we were channeling the same spirit that he was channeling back in the '80s, he just let us go."
Capturing the soul of Hellraiser's greatest hits

For the game, Saber Interactive aimed to capture the "soul" of the franchise, drawing not only from the recognizable visual elements established in the Hellraiser movies, but also from Clive Barker's original novella, The Hellbound Heart, which served as the source material for the franchise. "This game is a response, specifically to The Hellbound Heart, the first film, and Hellbound: Hellraiser 2, the second film," de Fault said. "So it's just the things that Clive was involved with that resonated really strongly with people back then. We wanted to make something that renewed that and had the same soul, but for a new medium and 40 years later."

Barker was also credited as an executive producer on the third and fourth Hellraiser movies, but had no active production or creative involvement in the franchise until 2022's Hellraiser reboot. That gap saw six Hellraiser movies released, although fans usually consider this period a low point for the franchise.
Saber Interactive isn't afraid of pushing ratings boards to the limits

From what we've seen so far, Hellraiser: Revival looks like it'll be going all in on the extreme subject matter of Barker's work. Saber Interactive has confirmed that the game is going to be gory and sexy, as the studio didn't want to compromise on their vision--even if that meant it faced the risk of being denied classification in several regions. Why go that far? Because doing anything less was seen as a disservice to Hellraiser fans.

"We knew what Hellraiser ought to be. We knew how disappointed Hellraiser fans would be if we did compromise, so it was just never really on the table," de Fault explained. "We wanted to pitch it at a point where I don't know if the executives would necessarily have agreed with this at the time, but we always felt like, if we get denied a rating in one or two places, we've probably done our job right. It was just important to us to do everything with purpose. All of the depraved stuff that you might encounter in the game, I think everything in there is defensible in terms of there's a reason it's there. It's not just for shock value. "It's like a good discomfort."
"Comforting discomfort," Esov added. So far, it looks like the game will be available in the US, at least, as it has received an ESRB rating .

While all of that comforting discomfort is designed with a purpose in mind, don't be too surprised if Hellraiser: Revival makes you reach for a bucket. One scene in particular might be hard to stomach, as de Fault described it as a moment of "consensual mutilation" in the game.

"There's a consensual mutilation scene. In early versions of this, we failed to adequately convey to players that this was consensual. So, some people came away thinking it wasn't and that it was pretty distressing, and so we had to course-correct that. I think our intent was fully realized in the game. There wasn't really anything we wanted to do that we scaled back or anything like that. We just had to correct the execution in some places."
Hellraiser: Revival takes place in the ancient year of 2006

Hellraiser: Revival is set in 2006, in the small town of Claireport. Saber Interactive chose this time period as a bridge between '80s Hellraiser and the modern era, while also ensuring there wouldn't be any "super high-techy stuff" to distract players. "We still wanted it to feel like an older franchise, but just without going all the way back to the '80s," de Fault added.

Like most Hellraiser movies, Revival revolves around a pair of sex freaks who get more than they bargained for when they use one of the infamous puzzle boxes created by the Cenobites--the all-new Genesis Configuration in this instance. Playing as Aiden, it'll be up to players to rescue his girlfriend Sunny from the Cenobites, and you can expect to run into Pinhead at several points in the story.

"He plays a really substantial role," de Fault explained. He appears near the start of the game with all the other Cenobites, responding to the fact that Aiden and his girlfriend, Sunny, have used one of the configuration boxes from the game during their sexual play. In Hellraiser fashion, [the Cenobites] demand a soul, and they take somebody away who happens to be Sunny. "I probably shouldn't go further than that, but Pinhead, you encounter him multiple times. The deal that you have with him has its twists and turns, and it evolves."
Pinhead is also voiced by Doug Bradley, the actor who played him in several Hellraiser movies over the decades.

While previous Hellraiser media revolved around the Lament Configuration puzzle box, the Genesis Configuration is a completely new creation for the game. It serves as both a plot device and a weapon, but to use it, you'll need to fuel it with the suffering of enemies and Aiden's own anguish. Saber Interactive isn't spilling the beans on how it fits into the overall story of Hellraiser: Revival, but they did tease that it was made for a specific purpose that will be revealed eventually.

"It's all in the name of this glorified violence, and basically, it gets powered by the suffering of yours and others," game director Emil Esov explained. "When there is suffering in the vicinity, you get more energy into the box, and you can perform these abilities."

Don't expect to be taking on iconic Cenobites in Hellraiser: Revival. They serve a variety of roles in the game, helping Aiden to unlock new powers for the Genesis Configuration or acting as unstoppable antagonists you'll have to escape. The female Cenobite--sometimes referred to as the Fallen because she was a nun who was drawn to sin in her human life--will also serve as a devil on Aiden's shoulder when she's not unlocking new powers for the Genesis Configuration.

There's no shortage of enemies to deal with in Hellraiser: Revival, as Aiden will regularly come into conflict with the "Unworthy Ones" from the Cult of the Scarlet Church. Denied access to the Labyrinth, the worshippers of Leviathan are dangerous, but they're still fragile mortals who can be shot, skewered, and burned to death.
Hellraiser: Revival's puzzles serve as a nice change of pace between all of the horror

So what kind of game is Hellraiser: Revival? Esov and de Fault described as being a "puzzle-moderate" game, as when Aiden ventures into the depths of the Labyrinth, players will have solve the deadly challenges within that structure.. "There is like two to two-and-a-half hours of Labyrinth gameplay, and there is no combat in the Labyrinth," Esov said. "We intentionally designed it so the Labyrinth itself is something that is menacing, that is scary. Sometimes it's going to be, traps. Other times, it's going to be you using the Genesis Configuration to actually manipulate the Labyrinth. And then, sometimes it's the combination of the two. It's puzzle-moderate, but it's nothing like brain-crunching puzzles that require a lot of focus.

"I think most of the puzzles are kind of 10-second to two-minute breathers between action or exploration sequences, that just force you to tickle your brain a little bit," De Fault added. "I'd say they occur fairly frequently, but they're not head-scratchers."

title: Saber Responds To AI Criticisms In Rideshare Game And Promises, “We Will Never Fire Someone And Replace Them With AI”
event_sentences: One of the biggest talking points in gaming today is the use of artificial intelligence, including generative AI. It's a hot-button issue, and few companies have faced the level of criticism about it as Saber has. The developer recently found itself in hot water after CEO Matthew Karch lashed out at Rideshare Stimulator's former writer who said they were laid off and replaced by ChatGPT.
Now, Saber's chief creative officer, Tim Willits, has addressed the situation as well, promising that, "We will never fire someone and replace them with AI."

For anyone just catching up, Rideshare Stimulator is an upcoming Saber game where players take on the role of an Uber- or Lyft-like driver and interact with them as they take them to their location. The developers freely admit to using generative AI in various capacities, and now Willits has shed more light on the situation. He said the game's main campaign features dialogue written by humans, but there is also a "free ride" mode where Rideshare Stimulator wants to be able to reference current events in the real world.
"We use AI to generate that because we want to do it so fast," Willits said, adding that the plan is for weekly or biweekly updates with this kind of AI-generated content.

Willits also clarified that some of Saber's other games, including the new Hellraiser, Turok, Stuntman, and Space Marine games, also do not use AI. Saber, like many other game companies, is experimenting with AI in various ways.

"We want to figure this new technology out, and we don't know exactly where it's gonna go, and our players don't know where it's gonna go, so we're all ... all of us are trying as a society to figure this out together," he said. "We want to experiment with it. I personally believe somebody [at] some game company will come up with such a brilliant idea, and we'll all be like, 'That's it.' We just need to get there."

When asked specifically about claims that Saber is firing people and replacing them with AI, Willits said this is not true. "I promise you we have never let anyone go and replaced them with AI. We hire people all the time," he said.

A spokesperson for Saber previously told PC Gamer that neither Saber nor Rideshare developer Unigine replaced any writers with AI for that game or any others. "In fact, Saber's staff of writers has tripled since 2023. Rideshare's story was written entirely by real people," the company said.
Rideshare's "experimental, free-ride mode" does use generative AI "by necessity," Saber said, because "the number of passengers in the game is infinite."

"We are firm believers in using AI tools to improve or enhance gameplay experiences and improve NPC behavior as we have done since Saber was founded in 2001. As the industry has continued to contract, Saber continues to hire. None of our 3000+ employees have to worry about being replaced by AI," the developer said.

The writer in question, Stella Sacco, said Karch reached out to "apologize unreservedly" for how he spoke about Sacco. Karch had said , "Stella who? I had to ask Claude because I have never spoken to her or seen her."
Sacco added in a statement that Karch said "he regretted escalating and how people online were speaking about me."

title: Gears Of War: E-Day Has A Battle Royale-Inspired PvP Mode Where You Can Strip The Flesh Off Enemies
event_sentences: "It's very obviously inspired by battle royale games, but it's on a Gear-sized PVP map," creative director Matt Searcy said to GameSpot. "At the beginning of the map, there's lots of mobility, teams are moving around, you're trading the Power Core back and forth. But as the map goes on, you see defensive teams start to build up a front around the player they're protecting. And then, in awesome Gears fashion, the thing you're going to hold puts you at a slight disadvantage. So we gave you a heavy weapon that's basically a giant battery pack, and if somebody gets close to you within a really tight range, you can strip all the flesh off their body with a charge attack."

Crucible is one of four PvP modes that will be available on launch day. The multiplayer options include traditional Team Deathmatch, Conquest, and Demolition, each of which has been reworked for E-Day. Team Deathmatch has a dynamic respawn system to move spawn locations closer to where fights are breaking out, Conquest puts its own spin on the classic King of the Hill experience, and Demolition revolves around teams planting bombs on enemy territory.

Gears of War: E-Day launches on October 6 for Xbox Series X|S and PC, and it'll also be a day-one release through Xbox Game Pass. For more on the game, you can read up on how The Coalition solved its biggest lore problem.

title: Saber Boss Reacts To The Death Of Physical Games And Rising Console Prices
event_sentences: 2026 has been full of big storylines in gaming, including Sony's announcement that it will end support for physical PlayStation game discs in 2028 and the trend of consoles getting increasingly expensive. Tim Willits, the chief creative officer at Saber Interactive, caught up with GameSpot at Gamescom this week to discuss these topics and offer up a bizarre-sounding possibility for an "AI box" for games.

He said he was "surprised how upset people were" about Sony ending support for physical game discs. Willits said he hasn't bought a physical game "in a long time" because he enjoys the convenience of digital games. Willits is not alone, as the share of digital game sales is growing at numerous companies.

At the same time, Sony continues to sell millions of physical game discs annually . Willits said Saber still makes "a lot of money" from physical games, especially in Europe, but the trends are different in North America, he observed.

Willits went on to say he had an interaction with someone recently who asked him to sign a copy of Doom 3, a game he worked on when he was with id Software. "So for me personally, I'll miss that in the future," he said.
An AI game box?
Willits said he thinks someone in the future might create some kind of "AI box" into which players can "upload all your games."
"So maybe someone will do that," he said.

Another major storyline in gaming in 2026 has been how video game consoles today are more expensive than ever . There are numerous reasons for this, including US President Donald Trump's tariffs, the AI-fueled impact on component and memory prices, and more.

Sony and Microsoft raised prices on PlayStation and Xbox consoles so much that the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S consoles are now $150+ more expensive than they were when they launched in 2020. Nintendo, meanwhile, is hiking the price of the Switch 2 in September.

For his part, Willits said it's "shocking how expensive" it has become to buy a new console today, adding that it will "be interesting to see" how Sony and Microsoft manage this as they look to release new consoles.

A new report from Ampere Analysis said that if next-gen consoles do, in fact, come in at $1,000 or more, that could have a dramatic, negative effect on the market. To be sure, Sony and Microsoft have yet to detail their plans for new consoles, so there is no word yet on how much they might cost or when they could be release.
In other news, Willits told GameSpot more about the company’s plans to use AI in game development and how the company claims it will never fire anyone and replace them with AI .

title: Arc Raiders is adding a camera mode as part of October's major update, but some fans need more proof that the game's not going to wither away
event_sentences: We're getting dribs and drabs of news about Arc Raiders ' upcoming major update which is scheduled for October. A new "high-level" challenge has been promised to returning players, alongside a frozen map full of new arcs, plus there'll also be the small addition of a photo mode.

"Time to remember your raids, cameras are coming to the Rust Belt in October," a new social media post reads. By the looks of things this will let players record all the weird, wonderful, and downright stupid antics they get up to during Arc Raiders sessions. The only problem is, well, that the games just aren't as enjoyable as they used to be.

Arc Raiders has had its issues with cheaters for almost as long as it's been out. While PvE lobbies are still ok, PvP is a swamp of bad actors right now, and it's only been getting worse the more decent people leave, meaning cheaters take up a bigger portion of the playerbase. Some are even throwing themselves in front of friendly fire just so they can trigger a self-defense clause and murder without consequence, you just can't win against these guys.

So with all things considered, players aren't exactly overjoyed about photo mode when the house is on fire. "Using number keys as a heal bind [has] been bugged since near launch," one player says , detailing how borked their hotkeys are. "But sure, let's add a fucking camera!"

The frustration with Arc Raiders is clear, but I have to say I don't think it's fair to completely write the October update off before we've been able to play it for ourselves. I think it actually makes sense that Embark hasn't given too much away far in advance, hype would peter out quickly otherwise. I'm actually really excited to see the October update for myself, I'd love for it to spur on another stretch of raiding.

That isn't to say, however, that the October update doesn't have a lot to prove. On release Embark promised a grand 10-year plan for Arc Raiders. It hasn't even been a year since then, and that promise seems to be teetering on the brink. October might be the developer's final chance to convince players that this game really does have enough to take it further, because I fear patience is running thin.

title: Grand Theft Auto 6 reveal live coverage: breaking down the Netflix 'extended look' event
event_sentences: After years of speculation and rumors, Rockstar has finally given us a deeper official look at Grand Theft Auto 6. (Unlike the various unofficial looks we've been getting courtesy of a certain vegetable .)
The GTA 6 "extended look" aired Thursday, August 27 on Netflix at 12 pm PDT. It'll be available on Rockstar's YouTube channel six hours after that time.

The 26-minute long video was a montage of gameplay clips, some very brief, others showing extended scenes from missions. Though there's still a lot we don't know, much has now been confirmed about GTA 6's gameplay—we're picking apart the details below.
GTA 6 is due out on consoles on November 19. There's frustratingly still no PC release date, and Rockstar is unlikely to speak on that anytime soon.
Ahead of the official GTA 6 reveal, someone who goes by "Cyberleek" has been releasing gameplay clips that apparently come from a build of the game they have continuous access to.
Here are some of the big details, with the caveat that we can't be sure exactly how recent Cyberleek's build is:
Your identity as it relates to police APBs is represented by three icons, which we've deduced probably refer to your clothing, face/hair, and car

I still think it's quite poor form for Rockstar to make fans subscribe to Netflix to see the reveal of a game they've probably already preordered. Yes, we can all just wait six hours for it to be posted on YouTube (and realistically, it'll be ripped from Netflix well before that), but it's the principle of the thing.

I don't expect to hear much, or possibly anything, about GTA Online, but even if it's omitted, the fact of its omission will be notable. Rockstar surely has big plans for its future, but given how closely GTA Online (and its roleplaying community in particular) is associated with PC gaming, I wonder if those plans will be withheld until the studio is ready to talk about the PC version of GTA 6 itself.

(Image credit: Rockstar Games) We've gone straight into gameplay with no preamble, which is nice. The reveal opens with Jason and Lucia arriving at a drug distributor for a pickup. Naturally, things go wrong: This kingpin has been betrayed by his partner, and police are incoming. A shootout follows.

The portrayal of Jason and Lucia as a relatable couple—Jason in this scene tries to hurry Lucia's outfit picking along—juxtaposes a little strangely with the GTA universe's goofiness. While Lucia's changing, Jason flips on the TV and we see a couple parody ads, like the one below advertising a 30,000 calorie sandwich made by slaughtering a prairie's worth of animals.

title: Star Citizen's Squadron 42 delayed again, this time to avoid 'the attention buzz saw of GTA 6' says Chris Roberts
event_sentences: We see games getting delayed all the time, but today's delay is particularly notable because this particular game was first supposed to come out in, ooh, let me check... Yep. All the way back in 2015.

Squadron 42, the long-awaited, celebrity-packed episodic singleplayer component of Star Citizen has been delayed once again. And why? This time, according to game director Chris Roberts, it's to avoid the media hubbub around another oft-delayed game: GTA 6.
"At CitizenCon 2024 we announced we would ship in 2026. Our plan was to release in Q4 around IAE," Roberts said in a post on the RSI website.

"But much like the rest of the industry there is no way I want to launch my spiritual successor to Wing Commander, a game that has had twelve years of blood, sweat and tears invested into it (we started Squadron 42 development in 2014 as 2013 was opening studios, hiring people and getting the Hangar module out for Star Citizen) launching into the attention buzz saw of GTA 6.
"While GTA 6 isn’t launching on PC this November, pretty much all outlets and most content creators will be all over it, not leaving a lot of room for other coverage," Roberts said.
"We have taken a look at the release windows at the start of 2027, and decided that Q2 provides a better time for Squadron 42 to release."

We've seen a lot of games getting out of the way of Rockstar's path, but pushing the release that far into 2027 suggests CIG just wants more time. And judging from the state of the recent disastrous Star Citizen livestream , it may need more time.

"I know a lot of you will be disappointed to not be playing Squadron 42 at the end of this year," Roberts said, "but it is the best thing for the project as it is truly something special and so needs to the opportunity to have the focus of the wider gaming world."

title: Cyberleek may have just cashed out on their GTA 6 leak, earning over $200,000 in the most predictable crypto rugpull ever performed
event_sentences: Since their first leaked GTA 6 gameplay video, Cyberleek used the uploaded illicit footage as a platform for users to buy and trade $CYBERLEEK, a token minted on the Solana blockchain. Eventually, Cyberleek allowed viewers to use the cryptocurrency to vote on the subject of their next leak video.

By doing so, Cyberleek claimed viewers would be supporting "a secret project" to fight for a generic slate of consumerist talking points , and that the funding would be "directed toward the infrastructure needed to strike, as well as the security and protection required to withstand the inevitable corporate counterattacks."

To understand what exactly happened here, let me offer some context about the token itself. It was minted by a walletholder on the Solana blockchain 12 days ago, and after its minting, the walletholder—presumably Cyberleek themself—placed the initial supply of the token along with an amount of an another cryptocurrency into what's called a "liquidity pool" on the Raydium platform, making that walletholder a "liquidity provider," or LP.

In the aftermath, the value of $CYBERLEEK has plunged by roughly 40% for anyone who made the questionable choice to acquire any. But that's not Cyberleek's problem anymore. They're sitting on a nice new chunk of change (which they'll presumably need for their eventual legal fees, if you can count that as a "secret project").
For the rest of us, let this be a valuable lesson: Don't listen when a weird onion on the internet says to buy his special secret money. Not again, anyway.

title: Looks like you can try DLSS 5 out today yourself
event_sentences: 🚨DLSS 5 Running On Control with renodxso one of the renodx guys has dlss 5 neural rendering (ai filter) running on control. This was using the dlss nr dll found in nba 2k27. They have it working on character models only so far. Theres 7 different styles, the video clip… pic.twitter.com/YlEFVCIPJC August 27, 2026

We know that DLSS 5 is due to arrive with us in the autumn time, but that release date feels a lot closer, with specific files being picked out of an early access version of NBA2K27 and dropped into Remedy's Control (via Notebookcheck ). The files in question have been found in the 2K ball-tossing title's PC version—which is currently playable for gamers who purchased the Deluxe or Ultra editions—and a modder from the RenoDX team has managed to inject it into Control with sliders.

The mod has been released in the RenoDX Discord channel and offers up seven different styles, which seem to range from conservative to full-on yasification. So far it's just aimed at the character models, but given the suggested performance hit from enabling it, you are going to want to limit its reach.

Looking into the Reddit chats about it, people are suggesting drops on an RTX 5070 Ti that take Control from 71 fps to 35 fps. That's a big hit, though we are talking about a pre-release feature in a game that it's not (yet?) designed for. When ray tracing still gets a lukewarm reception due to its performance impact, yet another resource-hogging feature will likely struggle for traction even outside the AI antipathy in gaming.

(Image credit: Anonymous) Then there's another uploaded image where you can slide between the DLSS 5 on and off versions of the character model, where it's far more extreme. But still, I don't think it looks bad. If you'd given me that Faden model from the outset natively, I'd have marvelled at Remedy making such a detailed character, especially given the company's obvious desire for photorealism in its characters. It still obviously retains the geometry, but this is far more of the AI beauty filter fear that large parts of the gaming community are concerned about with this feature's release.

I think the fact this has all been pulled together from one DLL file taken out of an early access game is impressive, and makes me think that the instant DLSS 5 gets released, we're going to see a whole lot of these mods out there giving gamers access to all the controls for a whole bunch of games… whether those game developers like it or not.

(Image credit: Future) One final thing to note is that the DLL file in question is noted as DLSSNR in the description, which suggests that DLSS 5 as the catch-all name for this AI game filter is going to change. Rebranding it as DLSS Neural Rendering feels far more suited to this feature, and might have led to less of a backlash at the start, where calling it DLSS 5 from the outset made it feel like this is just what the next version of DLSS is in its entirety.

title: Netflix is likely pleased as punch with the GTA 6 extended look, which more than doubled its web traffic
event_sentences: One of the more confusing elements of the Grand Theft Auto 6 extended look is the fact that it debuted on Netflix, of all sites. Why? While it's harder to pin down the reasons Take-Two went for it, I can at least suss out that Netflix is probably feeling very happy with its end of the bargain.

This was enough of a bump to cause issues for some viewers , though Netflix otherwise held up reasonably well . That's great news for the streaming platform, which has presumably been struggling to keep up with that ever-enshittifying perpetual growth mindset—introducing ads over the past few years, ramping up prices, and toying with generative AI to make those aforementioned ads even more annoying. We can, sadly, expect more of this in the future.

As for what Take-Two got out of it, it's hard to say, given CEO Strauss Zelnick has been tight-lipped on the particulars . It could be Netflix paid a lump sum to the publisher as part of the temporary exclusivity deal, though the kind of payout they'd have to offer Take-Two to get Zelnick interested would be pretty major, given Take-Two's worth an eye-watering $43.5 billion at the time of writing .

Then again, the preview was only Netflix-exclusive for six whole hours, meaning you'd likely only shell out for a new subscription if you were ravenous for more news—or just didn't want to spend an evening dodging spoilers before you sat down and watched the thing yourself. It is, after all, already on YouTube .

Which means that Take-Two had very little to lose by saying "yes" other than consumer goodwill. And given the self-styled "Robin Hood" of gaming (these airquotes are so heavy), Cyberleek, has seemingly grabbed the bag and ran ? I'm not sure the front against GTA 6 is particularly unified. Chances are that folks are going to buy this game regardless of what Take-Two does .

title: GTA 6 is adding a more nuanced version of Red Dead Redemption 2's honor system to ensure player characters aren't too 'all-powerful'
event_sentences: Two wrongs don't make a right, but one huge wrong and then a lot of little rights can make it feel better. According to Rockstar North's co-studio head Rob Nelson (via IGN ) GTA 6 will be getting this treatment, just a little bit more nuanced.

But here's where the nuance comes in: doing bad things doesn't necessarily count against your Criminal Profile. If you're in a situation where violence is the only logical and safe next step then sure, start shooting, but if you're the aggressor or have even escalated a situation beyond any reasonable amount? NPCs will remember that.

(Image credit: Rockstar) This isn't Rockstar trying to teach its players mortality, I think we all know it's too late for that, but it is an attempt to make Jason and Lucia's actions a little more realistic. "You are playing as criminals on the run, but the narrative is such that it makes most sense for them to do what they need to do while not drawing unnecessary attention (even though sometimes that happens)," Nelson explains.

title: After seeing what GTA 6 does to a PS5 we're even more desperate to see what the PC version has for us
event_sentences: But the hardware team has been poring over the released footage captured on a lowly PlayStation 5 and we've put our heads together to figure out what we think, and what extra bells and whistly things we want to see built into the eventual PC build of the game.

For right now, we have an admittedly beautifully looking game running at a peasant 30 fps frame rate, on a seven year-old Sony console. The top PC hardware of today is far beyond what the aging hardware inside the PS5 is capable of… even if right now the cost of admittance to the world of top PC hardware is inexcusably high. Who knows, maybe by the time GTA 6 is allowed to release on PC the RAMpocalypse will be over? Though that either means GTA 6 won't release on PC until maybe 2031 or the AI bubble pops sending us back into the economic stone age. Cheery thought.
GTA 6 PC release : When it might happen

As for the open world, I can spot some reflections and lighting that look like they're rendered in a pretty traditional way, rather than full RT. Look to the shiny floor in Lucia's apartment and the reflection of the windows, from the TV set, or the light coming through the blinds onto the kitchen countertop—we're not getting RT cranked to the max on PS5. Same goes for the storefronts we see Lucia holding up at gunpoint later in the gameplay trailer. Though the car chases look pretty lush out in the amber sun-lit tones of Vice City.

(Image credit: Rockstar) We're still trying to spot where effects are more faithfully reproduced out in the open world. We think we've maybe whittled it down to RT for reflections, used sparingly for cutscenes. Though it's definitely a challenge to make out with recorded gameplay going through YouTube's servers.

There do appear to be some RT reflections on the van, puddle, and window around the 16:40-16:50 mark. As Dave also pointed out to me, there's also a touch of what appears to be denoising in some places—on the rear of the van at, say, 16:10—but in other places, RT effects appear pretty low-key or non-existent. Like the molotov cocktail just moments before. A selective approach to balance the beauty of cutscenes and the demands of a massive open world? Makes sense, especially on the PS5's hardware.

With more firepower on PC, a few softer shadows wouldn't go amiss. Some indirect lighting, too, as the shadows look hard enough you could cut them with a knife at times. Presuming GTA 6 will follow in the footsteps of Red Dead Redemption 2 with DLSS support, we should get some help bear the brunt of the graphical load when it does launch on PC.

So, moody lighting, massively high contrast, and gorgeous vistas. It's impressive what can be achieved on this seven-year-old console hardware, no doubt about that; but with that in mind, I'm just more pumped for the PC version after watching this. GTA 6 looks like a game that has the potential to look absolutely stunning with more performance under the hood and when it's not curtailed by outgoing console hardware. It's screaming out for a cutting-edge GPU. It can't come to PC soon enough.

It's a confident move from Rockstar to just put up almost half an hour's worth of actual gameplay, and the lighting looks really quite striking… in stills. Every time I pause the trailer, I admire a little bit of the game's artistry, from its graffiti to the hair of its characters, and it makes the rundown nature of the first building really shine. How good that will be to play is a different matter, as the game's approach to realism does make those dark halls a little darker than I'd want, and without sufficient clarity to easily make out what's going on in an instant.
You can spot Rockstar's pretty incredible attention to detail in some reflections, like you can see Jason in the convex mirror at 12:09.
(Image credit: Rockstar) In motion, it looks surprisingly choppy for an official gameplay trailer.

Rockstar's attention to detail can be a double-edged sword though, as things like the fire on the car at 16:04 looking a tad flat or the lack of an accurate viewfinder in the camera at 20:17 make the world feel a little more plastic. These aren't things I would traditionally even care about, but it's Rockstar's approach to its world that makes them feel a little off. Rockstar's history, plus budget, make it the realistic open world maker, so it has become its unique cross to bear.

In fairness, the game looks undeniably good to me. Rockstar has the reputation for engaging, immersive, and realistic worlds for a reason, and the clarity of textures, plus strong lighting, makes GTA 6 look even more immersive and realistic than its predecessor. Whether or not it's as engaging will have to wait until we have it in our hands.

In motion, it looks surprisingly choppy for an official gameplay trailer. There's notable slowdown right after Jason enters the building at the start, and there are plenty of little sections where the flow of the game is just interrupted. But alas, that's the game running on a PlayStation 5, and we PC gamers have the ability to run this game at higher frame rates, especially when we consider the array of upscaling and frame generation. And Rockstar will have some time between the console and PC release to fine-tune the game too. That's the one benefit of us having to wait.

I'll always jump at a chance to add a pretentious word to my writing, so how about this one: chiaroscuro . Or, the contrast created between light and shade. It's interesting to see how often Rockstar plays with the difference between brightly lit streets and dimly lit interiors, or stark shiny highlights set against moody backdrops.

At points, I almost want to adjust the settings of my Mini LED monitor. The apartment raid at 5.25 switches from a grimy, fluorescent-lit hallway into a candle-lit dwelling with plenty of atmosphere, but also creates the sort of black-on-grey, mushy tones that make me squint to see anything that isn't directly lit. This is likely made worse by video compression, but there are plenty of darker moments that I feel would be difficult to read on anything other than a high-end display.

(Image credit: Rockstar) However, some of the brighter scenes are downright stunning. The meeting scene at the rooftop bar is striking, and the lighting of the character models themselves stands out. The soft shadow on Lucia's right arm as she approaches the bar at 9.55, the highlights in the character's hair. I'll be honest, this is downright impressive for a crowded scene in an open world game.

Impressive enough that some of the lesser elements stand out. The fountain on the left shows some pretty flat water effects, with the two jets looking a little out of place. Similarly, the overblown cigar smoke at 11.13 seems to come from a different era, which is all the more apparent when the rest of the scene is so beautifully rendered.

Perhaps some of these more incidental effects might be improved in a PC release—and some of the possibly-ray-traced puddles and car reflections seem like they could do with a whack from the PC hardware headroom stick, too. There are plenty of reflections going on here, but I'm not totally blown away by the shiny stuff overall.

(Image credit: Rockstar) It's also fairly apparent that there's a lot of upscaling in use, as evidenced by the odd bit of shimmering and the occasional fuzzy edge. With some proper PC firepower keeping the frame rate up behind the scenes (and thereby less upscaling assistance), it's possible that things will sharpen up further.

A lot of work seems to have gone into the hair rendering, which is shown in many different styles throughout the footage. However, individual hair strands are something that upscalers can traditionally struggle with, and I think there's some clear evidence of that. Particularly around the three minute mark, where a character's dreadlocks are shown lit from behind by fluorescent lights. They bounce and twist with verve, but the fringes look a little blurred and messy, likely due to the upscaling struggling with the finer strands.

I'm picking out small details, though. Little things. Honestly, GTA 6 looks even better in motion than I expected, although I can't help but feel it's going to be very demanding even at lower settings. Prepare thy graphics card? Mine is already quaking in its boots.

My first reaction to the GTA 6 extended gameplay preview is to marvel at the fact Rockstar has achieved this level of open world detail on lowly PS5 hardware (not even PS5 Pro) and my second is to pine for the inevitably grandeur the PC version will deliver when the company deigns to release it.

That's going to be the main thing the PC version will bring to the party—firstly more potential graphical horsepower with high-end GPUs, but also more mature upscaling options with DLSS and FSR really hitting their respective strides right now. You look at DLSS running in Ultra Performance mode at 4K and the visual fidelity, and more importantly the stability of the visuals, is pretty stunning, especially when you consider it's taking 921k pixels and turning them into 8.3 million pixels.

Love it or hate it, you're going to get some frame generation options for the PC release, too. By the time the game comes out all the GPU vendors will comfortably in their multi frame gen eras, and it's going to massively help on smoothing out the choppy gameplay you can see most especially at the start of the extended preview.

(Image credit: Rockstar) You may not like this, but I'm also pretty confident you're going to get some DLSS Neural Rendering when GTA 6 hits the PC, too. Having the PC version as a real showcase for all of Nvidia's features would be a real boon for the GPU maker AI company, and I wouldn't be surprised to see a ton of its developer relations team swarming all over Rockstar to get its AI filtering baked into the game.

But what about the first-person mode that made its debut in the PC release of GTA 5, will we see that making a comeback for this generation? We haven't seen it showcased in any of the leaks or preview gameplay, so it doesn't look like it's in the console release, but as the spiritual home of the FPS I could see it being another PC feature.

Whatever does or does not make it into the inevitable and inevitably delayed PC version of GTA 6, one thing this preview has done is made me pine ever more for the chance to throw an RTX 5090 at those visuals and see just how good it can look on the best gaming platform.

title: id Software's former co-owner says they absolutely would've used gen AI back in the day: 'John Carmack would be like making Skynet or something'
event_sentences: Generative AI is a hot-button topic in the industry, and for good reason—it's been kinda destructive, whether that's jacking up hardware prices or putting people out of a job —and while there have been some fairly mundane use cases that seem helpful, it's been hard to escape the sheer sense of mania that's built around its use. Or the bad PR, juiced out of the sheer exhaustion we've all had from executives promising the matrix or something .

So, naturally, it came up in a conversation with Tim Willits, the CCO of Saber Interactive and also the co-owner id Software from 1995-2019. Speaking to PC Gamer's Joshua Wolens at Gamescom 2026 , he notes that: "As most people know, we are experimenting with AI in future games. We don't have it here right now, but we announced [Rideshare Simulator] and I want to clarify things because there's some misconceptions."

If you're wondering why we're talking about a Rideshare sim, here's some context: Saber landed in hot water earlier this month over it, because it seemingly delayed its AI disclosures on Steam for a while , and was exposed as using AI by a former writer who claims they were booted off the team in favour of it.

That same writer was badmouthed by Saber's CEO Matthew Karch, who later apologised . Willits says that Rideshare's main campaign mode and all of its side missions are written by humans, and the AI components are only used for an optional game mode called Free Ride: "We're going to use AI for the passengers, so we can deliver new stories.

"So that is only possible if we use AI for that—this is an experiment. We at Saber want to figure out how we can use this technology, so we're doing it at a small scale to try to learn. We're like everyone else, we're just trying to figure this out. But there is no generative AI in our big titles. No Hellraiser, no Turok, none in Stuntman."

I feel like an asterisk has to hang over that "only possible"—while, yes, churning an infinite stream of dialogue for an optional mode is only possible with generative AI, a free ride mode with enough conversations for it to not grow stale absolutely could've been cobbled together with actual writers and voice actors. Sure, you'd run out eventually, but I don't think anyone's hungry to make Rideshare Simulator their forever game.

Still, Willits emphasises: "We want to experiment, and I do believe that there will be a company—I don't know who—but some game development company will create a game that uses AI in such an amazing way that everyone will be like, 'That's it, that's what we need to do'." He then goes on to joke that "someone needs to come up with the 'Half Life 2 of AI', something that's so amazing that it just launches some type of killer app."

I remain characteristically unconvinced, though in fairness to Willits, I do at least think that—if generative AI does find a use as the core of a videogame—it'll probably be a new genre of its own, rather than trying to create an infinite RPG with infinite NPCs. An act which would just shake out to make something unappealing and meaningless .

I'll eat my artificially-generated hat with a side of humble pie if Willits' "Half-Life 2 of AI" game materialises, but a lot of people have swung at that ball and missed, and each time I feel like the bat is a little smaller. Still, Willits says that id Software probably would've used generative AI if it was a thing back in the day—because the studio was always at the cutting edge.

"Yes! Oh, of course. I mean, look at what [id Software] has done. In 1999, when we released Quake 3, it required a graphics card, and we got so much hate for that. People said we were going to ruin the industry. Nobody was going to spend $100 on a video card, and it was the dumbest thing that anyone ever did … I know for sure back in the day if it was available, John Carmack would be like making Skynet or something."

Still, to be fair to Willits, he seems to share my view that the game'll have to prove that generative AI can change the industry itself, rather than via the promises of a CEO somewhere: "The games will speak for themselves, even in our experiment with Rideshare, I encourage people to check it out when it comes out, play it themselves. They may be like 'oh, this is cool! I like this'. And if they don't like it? Fine. And but the games speak for themselves."

title: Pulsar's new mouse is sliced in half to make it genuinely 'crazy-light'

title: All the key details about 'anime GTA' game Ananta
event_sentences: Ananta remained a mystery for many years, but it's finally got a solid 2027 release date. Plus, there's now plenty of proper gameplay footage and hands-on impressions to peruse in the meantime, letting us all in on the secret of what else "anime GTA" is actually offering.

From its release date, to characters, to gacha and gameplay, I'll explain everything you need to know about Ananta (previously Project Mugen), so you can decide if any of its approximately one million features are for you or not.
Ananta release date and (lack of) betas
(Image credit: NetEase) Ananta release date

After years of no-showing at big events, it finally turned up to Gamescom's 2026 Opening Night Live to announce that Ananta is releasing on January 15, 2027 for PC, PS5, and mobile. You can play it via Steam, or its own separate launcher.

There has never been an open beta for Ananta , and it's not looking like there will be one before the game's January launch either. That's uncommon for gacha games, but Ananta is developed by a NetEase studio, and NetEase's live service games don't tend to get open betas—just closed private testing. So all is (disappointingly) normal here.

It's worth keeping in mind that Ananta will likely dish out these rewards to every player at launch, not just those who pre-register. This is the norm for live service anime games, but there is a chance Ananta bucks this trend, as nothing's been confirmed yet.
Ananta Trailers
Latest trailer

As well as highlighting your main character, the Captain, and their crew's bizarre shenanigans about Nova City, Ananta's newest trailer revealed its second city: Chongxiao. Its other location, Nova City, seems more urban and Tokyo-inspired, while Chongxiao seems to be using China's Hangzhou as a reference. It's a little more tranquil, with scenic lakes, greenery, and historic architecture.
First trailer

If you want to know how it was revealed three years ago, you can check out Ananta's very first trailer above. Anana changed more than its name since then—its city and protagonist looked a lot different, and it had a more serious tone.
Ananta gameplay details

He found the influences of the Batman Arkham games, Sleeping Dogs, Uncharted, and Spider-Man pretty clear, but they all worked well enough. "This may be a game that does dozens of things acceptably well. And it made me laugh," he said. You can read Wes's full Ananta preview for more details.

While killing said baddies, you can whip out guns like an assault rifle and rocket launcher, or you could put your fists to the test and time hits and combos as enemies surround you—maybe use the environment to bash a head or two while you're at. If melee weapons are more your thing, bats, swords, tennis rackets, mallets, and golf clubs are also at your disposal. Add on each character's unique attacks (like Alan's ice yo-yos, Bansy's paintguns, and Taffy's motorbike-chucking), and you've got one very versatile combat system at play.

(Image credit: NetEase) Confirmed open-world activities include racing, dating, arcade mini-games, going to the gym, watching TV, shopping for new fits, customising houses, and picking up and carrying around chunky cats. For reasons. There's also a chance you might swap characters and catch one of your buds doing any of these things, as a GTA 6-style character switching system has been seen in trailers and demo gameplay.
Not at launch , but the developers have stated that the team is looking into a four-player co-op mode where you'd be able to complete missions or "dungeons" together.

(Image credit: NetEase) Despite all appearances, no, Ananta is not a gacha game . Well, at the very least, its characters aren't obtained from gacha pulls . Instead, they're all available completely for free by just playing through the game.

It is a free-to-play, live-service game, though, so Ananta will be looking to part you with your money somehow. Clothes, vehicles, and homes are the only confirmed cosmetics you'll buy with real-world money right now. But nobody knows 100% for sure if these cosmetics are available for outright purchase, or pulled through their own gacha systems. The only thing the developers have confirmed is that characters are not linked to gacha.
Wait, what's Project Mugen?

The title "Ananta" was only revealed in December 2024, before that, the game was solely referred to as Project Mugen (well, Project Mugen and "anime GTA" in some circles). So if you ever see a trailer or some gameplay for a game that looks mighty like Ananta, it's probably some pre- title reveal footage.
(Image credit: NetEase) A mix of trailers, social media posts, and the official website has revealed 16 Ananta characters so far:
Aileen - Maid cafe manager who utilises some sort of martial arts in combat.
Bansy - Graffiti artist who can use a paintball minigun and paint can grenades in combat.

Captain (Main character) - Pick between male or female presenting protagonists. The female Captain has gone missing in recent marketing, but as far as we know she's just MIA and not removed from the game.
Dila - White-haired lady "shrouded in mystery" who uses a claymore in battle and is also confirmed to have supernatural powers.
Lykaia - Fox lady who uses a two-handed spear-like weapon. She's both the Prime Minister of Nova City and Director of the Nova City Crime Agency (NCCA).
Taffy - The short, bunny-eared delivery girl seen in every trailer, and one of the founding members of your "Yeet Squad". Can use her motorbike in combat and for exploration.
A bat-wielding woman with a demon tail who dresses in red

Interestingly, it has been confirmed that each character has their own story, and we'll get to experience different lives depending on the character we're currently playing. That's 16 storylines already, if all of these characters are available at launch.

title: Fable director says they aren't 'scared of other big games' except one—it's GTA 6, in case you were living under a rock
event_sentences: Watching videogame studios try and bob and weave around Grand Theft Auto 6 's launch—especially when it was up in the air when exactly it'd come out—is a little like watching a flock of Marios (is that the correct plural noun? A mama mia of Marios?) all trying to dodge the same whomp.

"But the rationale for it is absolutely sound. I'm glad that we're avoiding that chaotic window.” For what it's worth, the window itself includes a ton of non-GTA stuff. This summer's been a touch dry on big new releases, but in the wider videogame industry you've got Onimusha: Way of the Sword , Blood of Dawnwalker , two Star Wars games, Marvel's Wolverine , Control Resonant , Gears of War: E-Day , and Phantom Blade Zero all before the year's even out.

But even Fulton cops that, yeah, the big one's the main reason: "We don't run scared of other big games. We're a big game ourselves. We hold ourselves to high standards. I'm happy to go toe-to-toe with a bunch of other games. There's just one that I'm happy to avoid entirely." Fair enough.

title: Rockstar has to 'be careful' about what GTA 6 picks to satirize because 'very specific political issues or memes will date fast'
event_sentences: It's certainly a tall order, especially right now, but if someone's able to do it I'm confident in Rockstar, who should be able to pull off some meta-commentary about the make-believe state of Leonida, based on Florida, and the US at large.

(Image credit: Rockstar) "That’s a question a lot of people ask: how do you deal with satire in today’s world?" Rockstar North's co-studio head, Ron Nelson, tells IGN . "I think there’s always stuff to satirize. As long as humans are humans, other humans will figure out ways to satirize what we do."

Sure, they'll always be people who will satirize the world around them, but the key here is doing it well enough that it doesn't make players' eyes permanently roll into the back of their heads, while also holding up against the test of time. Rockstar surely wants people to play and enjoy GTA 6 beyond 2026.

"We have to be careful that what we’re choosing to satirize is not going to feel dated in a weird way," Nelson explains. "I think those broader things are OK to satirize, but very specific political issues or memes will date fast. Even the way our characters speak, we think about it a lot so that they're not using extremely contemporary slang. Even though our characters are a certain age, they need to feel somewhat timeless."
That probably means we won't be seeing any brainrot or references to the orange man in GTA 6, and you know what? Thank god—sometimes art doesn't need to fully imitate life.

title: Chinese memory maker YMTC wants to dethrone Samsung and SK hynix by the end of 2027
event_sentences: According to the Financial Times , citing "two people with knowledge of the matter", YMTC told investors that it wants to be the leader in the market (ahead of Samsung and SK hynix) by the end of 2027. That's a pretty bold claim considering it would need to more than double its current market share.

According to Counterpoint Research , YMTC holds a 13% market share, while NAND memory leader Samsung holds 29%. In fairness, though, YMTC does appear to be building up its infrastructure to handle growth.

In April, it was reported that YMTC was aiming to more than double its wafer production . It would do so by building two additional foundries and finishing the build of a third foundry that was already under construction.

NAND memory is a very lucrative business right now. In the first quarter of 2026, NAND flash memory makers earned $46 billion in revenue, which is over 3.5 times what they made in the same quarter last year. NAND memory is only getting more expensive, and data centers are mopping it all up to train AIs and store all that data. But YMTC has even had a win in the consumer market, seemingly putting its SSDs into some Lenovo laptops . That's something it may have struggled to do previously, if it weren't for memory and storage supplies being so limited.
